A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

callosal section in the rat facilitates LRRD by reducing the number of trials needed to learn the task, and by increasing the number of trials in which the correct response is made on the first trial.

callosal section facilitates the learning of LRRD, and that the anterior and posterior portions of the callo-sum appear to contribute to the facilitatory effect in a manner that is independent of each other.

callosal section, in addition to its well-documented effect on the integration of lateral information in sensory processing, also facilitates the development of left-right response differentiation by allowing the development of lateral specialization of the motor system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
partial callosotomy is a useful technique for investigating the functional significance of the corpus callosal interhemispheric connections.
partial callosotomy can produce facilitatory effects in the LRRD paradigm, but that these effects do not occur in all rats and do not produce as strong a facilitatory effect as total callosotomy.
callosal function is not unitary but rather is composed of a number of separable processes, some of which may be independent of others.
